mock.title: How we glaze our stoneware
mock.dek: Every Northwind mug and bowl passes through two firings and three pairs of hands. Here is what happens between the wheel and your kitchen shelf.
mock.coverCaption: Bisqueware waiting for its glaze bath in the Portland studio.

content.text: Glazing is the step people ask us about most, and the one we rush least. A glaze is a thin layer of glass fused to the clay at 2,264 °F. Get it right and the surface stays food-safe and dishwasher-proof for decades.
Every piece is bisque fired first, to 1,832 °F. That leaves the clay hard enough to handle but porous enough to drink up glaze evenly. Then comes the part that takes practice:
Wax the foot so the glaze stops 5 mm above the base.
Dip for a slow count of three. Thicker coats pool in the curve of a bowl and turn glossy.
Wipe, dry overnight, then load the glaze kiln shelf by shelf.
The kiln always has the last word. We just try to give it a good argument.
is reactive, so no two mugs match exactly. That is why we stamp the batch code, such as
Why every mug looks slightly different
The same glaze bucket can give three different results depending on where a piece sits in the kiln. Hotter shelves near the burners melt the glaze further, so the speckle spreads and the rim darkens.

attrs.alt: Three glazed mugs in blue-grey, oat and slate on a linen cloth
attrs.title: Left to right: Fjord, Oat and Slate, all from kiln batch FJ-26-09.

content.text: Climb slowly to 1,112 °F so trapped water can escape.
Hold at 2,264 °F for 15 minutes to heal pinholes.

content.text: US orders leave our Portland studio within 2 business days and arrive 2 to 4 days later. Canadian and EU orders take 5 to 9 business days. Made-to-order knitwear ships in about 3 weeks, and the product page always says so.

items.question: Can I return something that isn't right?

content.text: Yes. You have 30 days to send back anything unused, in its original packaging. US returns are free with the prepaid label in your parcel. Seconds and personalised pieces can't be returned unless they arrive damaged.

items.question: Why does my mug look different from the photo?

content.text: Every piece is glazed by hand and fired in small batches, so colour and speckle vary from kiln to kiln. We photograph a typical piece, and the card in your box tells you which batch yours came from.

items.question: How should I wash wool and lambswool?

content.text: Air it more, wash it less. When it does need a wash, hand wash cool with a wool detergent, press out the water in a towel and dry flat away from the radiator.

items.question: Are your ceramics dishwasher and microwave safe?

content.text: Our stoneware is dishwasher, microwave and oven safe up to 400°F. Pieces with a gold rim or raw clay base are hand wash only, which is noted on the product page.
Every order ships in recycled tissue and a plain kraft box. Add a handwritten card at checkout for $4, and we leave prices off the packing slip.

content.text: Northwind started in 2014 with one wheel in a Portland garage and a simple rule: make fewer things, and make them to last. Today a team of twelve designs every piece in Oregon and works with four family-run workshops across Europe.
We never run seasonal sales. Instead we price fairly all year, and we repair what we sell.

tabs.label: Knitwear
tabs.heading: Wash less, air more

content.text: Wool resists odour on its own. Most of the time, a night on a hanger by an open window is all a jumper needs.

tabs.linkLabel: Shop wool wash and cedar blocks

content.text: Our stoneware is fired to 2,264°F, so it is dishwasher, microwave and oven safe to 400°F. Pieces with a gold rim or raw clay foot are hand wash only.

tabs.label: Wood & boards
tabs.heading: Oil it when it looks thirsty

content.text: Wash with warm soapy water, dry upright and never soak. Every few weeks, rub in a little board oil and leave it overnight.
Wash at 105°F with like colours, skip the fabric softener and line dry. Iron while slightly damp if you like it crisp.
